$comment: PROPOSED English copy for what this design adds. Live text only: none of it is drawn into an illustration. Frontend owns interface wording and the game owner owns rule statements; every line that states a rule cites the rule source it paraphrases, and every cited source is a file in this branch. Nothing here is approved. The nine role cards are Designer's draft (open decision DSN-D17). Frontend said on PR #57, on 7 October 2026, that it will draft the eight cards that had none, from the approved rule sources and from what the connected client already says of each action: these lines are offered to that draft and do not replace it. Where the two differ, Frontend's wording stands. The names of actions and of what a seat knows follow the connected client's copy as read on agent/frontend-hosted-feedback at b31e957 (Rescue, Disable, Supply, Protection, Scan, Code attempt). Where an approved in-person V1 decision on the landing candidate bears on a line, its `note` says so, because that overlay is not in this branch's base and cannot be cited here.

Officer.name: Officer
Officer.summary: You start with one ordinary shot. You may register it during your own turn, from Round 1.
Officer.limit: One ordinary shot for the whole match.
Officer.mustNotSay: Nothing about identifying or guessing another player's faction or role: that step is archived (rules/overlays/direct-shot-decision.json). “Ordinary” is there because the final showdown gives every participant a special shot of its own (rules/overlays/final-showdown-decision.json): the card must not read as if the Officer had none left for it.

Insider.name: Insider
Insider.summary: At the start you are shown three players. One of them is the Undercover, one the Alien and one the Cracker.
Insider.limit: You are not told which of them holds which.
Insider.note: The three players themselves are private data of the seat's own view, not copy.

Cracker.name: Cracker
Cracker.summary: Rescue: choose one player. At the end of the round, if that player is Injured, they become Healthy.
Cracker.limit: Two rescues for the whole match. A rescue cannot bring back an Eliminated player.
Cracker.note: The card does not say where the player to rescue must be: the server's own target list does. The base sources require the same location and give the Cracker access to the Hospital; approved decision V1-05 makes rescuing a player in the Hospital from Room A or Room B an explicit exception, and V1-15 says a rescue that heals nobody is still used up. Both are on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

Blue Disabler.name: Blue Disabler
Blue Disabler.summary: Disable: choose a player in your location. If it takes effect, a Healthy player becomes Injured and an Injured player is Eliminated.
Blue Disabler.limit: One use for the whole match.
Blue Disabler.note: “If it takes effect” is there because Protection can cancel a Disable; the card must not promise an outcome. Approved decision V1-13 adds that the target is another player, and V1-15 that the use is reserved when the action is accepted: both are on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

Supplier.name: Supplier
Supplier.summary: In Round 3, choose two different players in your location. Each receives one ordinary weapon, usable in Round 4 or 5.
Supplier.note: The card does not say whether fewer than two may be chosen, or whether the Supplier may be one of them: the rule source says “two distinct recipients” and Game Balance has both questions open (D11, D12). Approved decision V1-16 adds who learns of a grant (each recipient and the Supplier, and nobody else) and that an Officer may receive a weapon they cannot use. It is on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

Undercover.name: Undercover
Undercover.summary: Protection: choose a Healthy or Injured player in your location. You may choose yourself. It becomes active at the start of the next normal round.
Undercover.limit: A player can receive Protection only once in a match. You also hold one ordinary weapon, usable in Round 4 or 5.
Undercover.also: In a Standard Hack you may lie.
Undercover.note: The card says nothing about how often Protection may be given: the rule sources limit how often a player may receive it, not how often the Undercover may give it. It says nothing about what a Protection blocked or whether it was used up. Approved decision V1-17 makes that known to the Undercover alone, as facts of the seat's own view, and to nobody else: it is on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

Hacker.name: Hacker
Hacker.summary: You know who the Undercover is. Scan: choose a player in your location, or yourself, and guess the faction. If the guess is right, you learn whether that player's number is in the Code.
Hacker.limit: One Scan each round, and a wrong guess tells you nothing. In Round 5 you have one Code attempt: four players, in any order.
Hacker.note: The guess here is the Scan's own, which the rule sources keep; it is not the identification step of a shot, which is archived. Approved decision V1-14 adds that a Scan is used up when it is accepted and answers at once: it is on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

Red Disabler.name: Red Disabler
Red Disabler.summary: Disable: choose a player in your location. If it takes effect, a Healthy player becomes Injured and an Injured player is Eliminated.
Red Disabler.limit: One use for the whole match. You hold no ordinary weapon.
Red Disabler.note: As for the Blue Disabler. Approved decisions V1-13 and V1-15 are on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

Alien.name: Alien
Alien.summary: You know the whole Code from the start. If the Blue team wins and you are not Eliminated, you win too.
Alien.limit: If the Red team wins, you do not. If both teams are eliminated at the same time and you are not, you win alone.
Alien.also: In a Standard Hack you may lie.
Alien.note: The Code itself is private data of the seat's own view, not copy. Approved decision V1-19 says what “at the same time” means: it is on codex/v1-connected-merge-candidate at 71dfd02 (rules/overlays/in-person-v1-owner-decisions-2026-10-06.json), which is not in this branch's base.

resourcePip.note: Accessible names for the pip. Each repeats what the card's status word already says; none is an outcome. “Shot used” is drawn by no state in protocol 1, which has no field for it (DSN-D02).

privateHandle.note: The handle's visible word never changes with role, turn or availability. Frontend's Show/Hide button labels stay as they are.

table.boardSyntheticLabel: Synthetic layout state. Not a match.

syntheticStudies.note: mothership:dev-only. Lettering for the two synthetic studies only, read by studies.html. No approved fact exists for either word; neither may appear in a connected match.

seatTag.note: PROPOSED, for the two public facts of DSN-REQ-6. Where a seat has a name, its tag is the seat number and the name as two parts. The prefix and the separator are for assistive technology only: a tag is read aloud as “Player 7, Ada” and looks like the number in a chip followed by the name. Sentences that name a seat (“Register a shot at Player 2?”) are Frontend's to reword once names exist.

character.note: PROPOSED call signs, used only to tell the nine characters apart while one is being chosen, and as the accessible name of each choice. A call sign is not a player's name and is never shown on the board.
